note: Adherence briefs (#419): tasks that can't be done well without API a model is unlikely to have seen, or a contract that's easy to get wrong. Kept apart from the distinctiveness benchmark's eight briefs, which stay the control for 'does new guidance hurt the easy cases'. Same shape, so evals/distinctiveness/generate.mjs runs them with --briefs.

briefs.contract: errors linked from a summary; a required choice; one primary
briefs.text: Build an appointment request form for a dental clinic. People choose one appointment type (check-up, hygiene or a problem tooth), give their name, email and a preferred date, and send the request. Choosing a type is required. If anything is missing when they press send, list what's wrong at the top, with links to each field, and keep what they typed. Use realistic sample data; there is no backend.

briefs.contract: a refused move shown as failed with the reason, not silently reverted
briefs.text: Build a kanban board for a support team with To do, In progress and Done columns, and cards people can move between columns with the mouse and the keyboard. The server sometimes refuses a move (for example, In progress is full at three cards): when it does, show that the move failed and why, and put the card back. Simulate the server; there is no backend.

briefs.contract: proposed isn't pending; nothing saved before Accept
briefs.text: Build a customer record screen for a B2B billing tool, showing the customer's company name, billing email, plan and account owner. An assistant has proposed two changes (a new billing email and a different account owner). Show each proposal next to the current value, and let a person accept or reject each one. Nothing changes until they accept. Simulate saving; there is no backend.

briefs.contract: Meter format formats a number (#447); no pie charts; a chart that says one thing
briefs.text: Build a usage page for a file storage product. Show storage used against the plan's quota (412 GB of 500 GB), seats used (18 of 25), and a chart of storage used each day last month that makes clear whether usage is growing. Use realistic sample data; there is no backend.
